newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower, cement share falls.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower, cement share falls.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower with losers led by cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped a barely noticeable 0.03 percent, ending at 13,509.10 on a trading volume of 1.1 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB index fell 0.26 percent, meanwhile, closing at 860.75 on a lower-than-average volume of just 710 million pesos.
Cementos Caribe, which dropped 4.64 percent to close at 3,900 pesos per share, weighed heavily on the IBB.
Brokers attributed the fall and a 1.13 percent drop in heavily-traded Banco de Colombia, which ended the day at 435 pesos a share, to profit-taking.

Brewer Bavaria SA, which fell 9.74 percent in Bogota on Friday, dropped an additional 0.39 percent, ending at 3,785 pesos a share. The day's few winners included Banco de Bogota, which ended up 1.44 percent at 5,960 pesos per share and Cementos Argos, which rose 0.18 percent to close at 5,360 pesos.
Brokers said the market was extremely quiet and hopes that foreign funds would turn it around had been put on hold by many, at least temporarily, because of a "Catch-22" type situation.

"There are foreign funds that want to get in (and buy) but they can't find any sellers offering large blocks of shares because prices too low," one broker said in a telephone interview. He and others said a recent fall in 90-day CD rates to their lowest level in two years were positive for equities, however.
